name: Chimera 0.3.0
body:
# Chimera 0.3.0 (alpha)

New firmware for the PreenFM3: four sound engines (ALGO, MODAL, VA and TAPE), six parts, and the ORBIT sequencer. This is an early test version.

> **USB MIDI and USB audio are verified on Linux only.** They should work without a driver on macOS and Windows (Chimera is a class-compliant USB MIDI and audio device), but they haven't been tried there. If you use a Mac or Windows, please tell us in a [new issue](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases/issues/new/choose) whether the unit shows up, plays MIDI and records audio.
>
> Computer sleep and unplugging and replugging the USB cable haven't been tried with the unit either: please report whether USB MIDI and audio come back afterwards. Starting and stopping USB audio has been tried and works.

## What to download

- `CHIMERA.BIN`: the firmware.
- `CHIMERA.BK2`: the rest of the firmware (Chimera installs it from the card on its first start).
- `factory-v1.zip`: 128 sounds, the TAPE sources they play, 4 demo songs and the SUGGEST controller map.

## Install

The same steps install Chimera for the first time and update it from 0.2 or 0.1. The [README](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases#installing-chimera) has them with pictures.

1. Unzip `factory-v1.zip`. It unzips to one folder, **CHIMERA**.
2. Turn the PreenFM3 off. Hold **MENU** and turn it on: the bootloader should read `pfm3 BootLoader 1.09`.
3. Press **button 3** (SD card access). The card shows up on your computer like a USB stick. It stays inside the PreenFM3.
4. Copy `CHIMERA.BIN` and `CHIMERA.BK2` to the top of the card, not into a folder. If older copies are there, choose **Replace**.
5. Copy the factory set:
   - If the card has no **CHIMERA** folder, copy the whole unzipped **CHIMERA** folder onto it.
   - If it has one, copy folder by folder instead (on a Mac, replacing a whole folder throws away what was in it):
     - **SOUNDS** and **PROJECTS**: copy the files inside into the folders of the same name, choosing **Replace**.
     - **MAPS** (new in this release): if the card has no MAPS folder, copy the whole folder across. If it has one, copy the files inside, choosing **Replace**: that puts back the factory SUGGEST map and leaves your own maps alone.
     - **TAPES**: if the card has no TAPES folder, copy the whole folder across. If it has one, copy the files inside and choose **Skip** for any `.SRC` file already there. A source's name is its contents' checksum, so the one on the card is the same, and Chimera keeps it read-only.
   - The demo songs take the first 4 project slots. If you saved songs of your own there, copy them to your computer first.
6. Eject the card on your computer and press **MENU** to leave SD card access.
7. Step through the files with **−** and **+** until the bootloader shows `CHIMERA.BIN`, and press **button 1** (flash).
8. Chimera starts, finds `CHIMERA.BK2` on the card and installs it. It shows **DON'T POWER OFF** while it steps through ERASING, WRITING and SEALING, then carries on by itself. If the power goes off during the install, the next start installs it again.

If `CHIMERA.BK2` is missing or from another version, the Parts, ORBIT and the effects make no sound, Chimera ignores MIDI in, and the screens say **UPDATE** or **NEEDS UPDATE**. Copy the `CHIMERA.BK2` from this release onto the card and restart.

To find the sounds: press **EDIT + B1**, then turn **encoder 2** to the **FACTORY** tab.

### Coming from 0.2

- Copy both `CHIMERA.BIN` and `CHIMERA.BK2` from this release. `CHIMERA.BK2` now also holds ALGO, MODAL, the delay, the chorus and most of MIDI, so a 0.2 `CHIMERA.BK2` leaves them silent.
- Your projects and Sounds on the card stay. A Sound saved in 0.2 loads as before; a new Sound gets the mod wheel's vibrato route (see Modulation below).
- On Windows, the first time you connect the unit over USB after updating, Windows may set up its driver again, because the unit's USB layout changed. Let it finish, then pick **Chimera** again in your music software.
- The bootloader is unchanged. Chimera still needs the stock bootloader 1.09 and never writes to it.

## Demo songs

- **REVERB ROOMS**: Turn TYPE through QUAD, ROOM and HALL.
- **REVERB BLOOM**: Hold slow chords, then turn TYPE from BLOOM to REVERSE.
- **REVERB GATE**: Play short, sharp notes: the gate cuts every tail, the echoes too.
- **CHORUS DELAY**: Turn CHORUS through I, II and I+II.

## Voices

Chimera has 8 voices in all, shared by the six Parts. Each note costs a share of the processor that depends on its Sound: the engine, the model, the filter and the FX slot. A note gets a voice only if its cost fits in what is left, so a light Sound plays all 8 and a heavy one fewer.

Voices one Part gets on its own on the rev V chip, beside the TAPE delay and the QUAD reverb, with ORBIT stopped:

| Sound type | Example | Voices |
|---|---|---|
| ALGO, one or two operators | DRIFT ORGAN | 8 |
| ALGO, typical | AIR RAID | 7 |
| ALGO, heaviest | SOFT HORNS | 3 |
| ALGO with formants | NULL CHOIR | 4 |
| VA on the 2040 | SOLO PORTA | 7 |
| VA with FUZZ | INIT VA, FX FUZZ | 6 |
| VA on the LADDER with FOLD | GROWL BASS | 5 |
| MODAL STRING | NYLON | 8 |
| MODAL BOWED | CELLO SWELL | 8 |
| MODAL BANK | GAMELAN | 3 |
| TAPE one-shot or loop | HARP HIT, PAD LOOP | 8 |
| TAPE STRETCH GRAIN | VOICE STRETCH | 5 |

The delay's GRAIN type and the ROOM, HALL and BLOOM reverbs cost about a voice: with one of them on, many Sounds play one voice fewer.

These counts are for the rev V chip (480 MHz). A rev Y chip runs at 400 MHz and has less to share, so heavier Sounds play fewer voices. SETTINGS › SYSTEM › ABOUT shows which chip yours has.

## What's new in 0.3

The new guides: [MIDI control](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases/blob/main/MIDI.md), [Tuning](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases/blob/main/TUNING.md) and the [NRPN chart](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases/blob/main/NRPN.md).

### MIDI control

- Each Part has its own MIDI map of up to 16 bindings, kept in its Sound. A binding's control can be a CC, a 14-bit CC pair (`CC 2+34`), an NRPN (`NRPN 10:3`), channel PRESSURE or a SysEx message.
- Learn (**MIX + SEQ**) listens on after the first move and works out what kind of control it hears: `ABSOLUTE`, a relative encoding such as `RELATIVE · TWOS COMPLEMENT`, `BUTTON`, `14-BIT CC` or `INC DEC`.
- While learn listens, the value line reads `TURN IT RIGHT, THEN LEFT`, then shows the guess, and the hint reads `MIX + SEQ  DONE` once it is sure.
- Learn says why it refuses: `NOT MAPPABLE`, `CC 21 ON CH 3, PART ON CH 1`, `CC 64 RESERVED` or `MAP FULL`.
- The MIDI MAP page (SETTINGS › PART › MIDI MAP) reads B CONTROL, C MIN, D MAX, E INPUT and F ECHO, and spells out the bar's binding in full words under the list.
- E INPUT sets how a control moves its cell: `JUMP`, `PICKUP`, `SCALE`, `TWOS COMP`, `OFFSET`, `SIGNED`, `SIGNED 2`, `INC DEC`, `MOMENTARY` or `TOGGLE`.
- PICKUP waits until the knob reaches the cell's value, and the value line says `MOVE THE KNOB UP TO PICK UP` (or `DOWN`) while it waits.
- SCALE moves the cell at once, scaled so the knob and the value meet at the ends.
- A relative encoder turns the cell exactly as Chimera's own encoder does, one step a detent.
- A button binding is held-is-MAX (`MOMENTARY`) or flips between MIN and MAX on each press (`TOGGLE`).
- Every stored parameter has a fixed NRPN address that works with no binding at all.
- New guide page: the [NRPN chart](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases/blob/main/NRPN.md), every address by engine and block, for a sequencer's or DAW's instrument definition.
- Every Part answers the General MIDI CCs on its own channel, with no binding: CC 7 LEVEL, 10 PAN, 11 expression, 71 resonance, 72 release, 73 attack, 74 cutoff, 91 REVERB send, 93 CHORUS send and 94 DELAY send.
- CC 72 and 73 shift the release and attack from the Sound's own, 64 being the Sound as it is: every operator's on ALGO, ENV 1's on VA and TAPE, DAMP on MODAL (release only).
- What the built-in CCs move is what you see and save: the cells show the shifted values, and saving keeps them.
- Expression (CC 11) turns the whole Part down from its LEVEL, sends included. It is playing, not editing: never saved, no `*`, back at 127 after a project load or a Reset All Controllers.
- A binding on the same CC, in the Sound or the controller map, wins over the built-in CC.
- New cell D **BUILT-IN** on SETTINGS › MIDI CONFIG › CONTROL CHANNELS, `ON` by default, turns the built-in CCs off.
- With MPE, CC 74 on a zone's master channel is SLIDE only and leaves the cutoff alone.
- Reset All Controllers (CC 121) also resets expression and takes attack and release back to 64.
- Bindings can drive the master FX's continuous knobs (CHORUS, DELAY, REVERB and MASTER) and ORBIT's ring amounts: HITS, ROTATE, CHANCE, MUTATE, GATE, VEL, ACCENT and OCTAVE.
- **MIX + SEQ** learns on the master FX pages and the ORBIT pages too.
- MIDI MAP names a master FX or ORBIT target's block first, for example `REVERB MIX` or `RING 1 CHANCE`.
- A binding to the master FX or ORBIT lives in the map of the Part it was learned on and listens on that Part's channel.
- RPN 0 sets the Part's BEND range.
- Reset All Controllers (CC 121) resets the pedal, the bend, the mod wheel, pressure and CC 74.
- A CC lands while a Sound is saved to the LIBRARY or a list is read from the card; CCs wait only while a load replaces the Sound.

### SysEx controllers

- Old programmers and hardware editors that edit a synth by SysEx can drive Chimera's cells, learned with **MIX + SEQ** like a CC.
- Learn compares two of the box's messages to find the byte the value sits in, reads a two-byte value as 14-bit, and recognises a Roland-style checksum.
- A SysEx binding reads `SYSEX 9` on MIDI MAP (the value's byte, F0 counted first), is always absolute `JUMP`, glides like a CC and has no ECHO.
- A SysEx binding listens on every Part whose Sound holds it, whatever the channel.

### Controller maps

- A Part can play a named controller map kept on the card, apart from any Sound or project, so a controller is set up once for every project.
- MIDI MAP's first row, `CONTROLLER`, picks the Part's map: turn B through `NONE` and the maps on the card.
- A map has a shared section and one section per engine, so changing the Part's engine swaps the engine rows by itself.
- The Sound's own rows win a control; the map's row on the same control is dimmed.
- EDIT on `CONTROLLER` saves the Part's rows into a map through NAMING. A save that would give an engine more than 16 rows says `MAP FULL`; a clash with another map's files says `NAME TAKEN`.
- The project remembers each Part's map by name and reads it from the card again on every load.
- A map's rows show `IN <name>` on their spelled-out line, and B to F edit them as on a Sound's row; the change is written to the map on the card.
- **MIX + MINUS** on a map row asks, then removes the row from the map on the card.
- **MIX + EDIT** on `CONTROLLER` renames the picked map (`RENAME MAP`), and every Part playing it follows.
- **MIX + MINUS** on `CONTROLLER` asks `DELETE MAP?` and deletes the map; every Part that played it plays `NONE`.
- With a map picked, `CONTROLLER`'s lines read `MIX+EDIT RENAME` and `EDIT SAVE  MIX+MINUS DELETE`.
- A map save, rename or delete asked for while another waits says `CARD BUSY`.
- A map row whose map has left the card says `FILE NOT FOUND` and writes nothing.
- The factory set holds **SUGGEST**, a controller map for any box of knobs or faders: CC 20 to 29 play each engine's ten main controls by role (CC 20 the main timbre knob, 21 the second, 29 the character), and CC 14, 15 and 85 to 88 play LFO 1 RATE and DEPTH, ENV 2 LEVEL, the glide time and the FX slot on every engine. Its CCs meet none of the built-in ones.
- MIDI MAP lists up to 16 maps; with more on the card it says `CARD HOLDS MORE: 16 SHOWN`.
- Maps are card files in `/CHIMERA/MAPS`, a pair a map, so you can copy them to and from your computer through SD card access.

### KEEP MAP

- **MIX + PLUS** on MIDI MAP's `CONTROLLER` row turns KEEP MAP on or off for the Part; the line reads `MIX + PLUS KEEP MAP OFF` or `ON`.
- With KEEP MAP on, every Sound load keeps the Part's own rows instead of the loaded Sound's.
- Kept rows don't count as an edit, so a Sound loaded this way shows no `*` and the next load asks nothing.
- KEEP MAP is off for every Part after a project load or a restart.

### CONTROL CHANNELS

- New page SETTINGS › MIDI CONFIG › CONTROL CHANNELS sets three channels, MIXER, SEQ and AUTO, each `OFF` (the default) or 1 to 16.
- MIXER's channel moves each Part's LEVEL, PAN and sends and the CHORUS, DELAY, REVERB and compressor knobs by a fixed CC chart, gliding as a knob does.
- SEQUENCER's channel drives ORBIT by a fixed chart: PLAY/STOP, each ring's ON/OFF, CHANCE and STEPS, KEY and SCALE.
- A note on SEQUENCER's channel sets ORBIT's KEY to its pitch class.
- AUTO's channel plays whichever Part you are on; a held note or pedal stays with the Part that started it.
- A Part's own channel wins over a CONTROL channel, MIXER wins over SEQUENCER and SEQUENCER over AUTO. A losing cell is dimmed and the focus band reads `A PART HAS THIS CHANNEL`.
- Learn never binds on MIXER's or SEQUENCER's channel.

### MPE

- MPE controllers play Chimera note by note, in a lower zone (master channel 1) and an upper zone (master channel 16).
- A zone's notes play the Parts on its master channel.
- Each note's own pitch bend, pressure and CC 74 move that note alone, gliding and never stepping.
- The master channel's bend, wheel, pressure, CC 74, sustain pedal and All Notes Off reach every note in the zone.
- An MPE controller's configuration message (RPN 6) sets its zone and a bend range of 48 semitones.
- New page SETTINGS › MIDI CONFIG › MPE sets the zones by hand: LOWER, L BEND, UPPER and U BEND.

### Program change

- A program change loads a Sound into every Part on its channel. Turn it on at SETTINGS › MIDI CONFIG › SYNC, B **PROGRAM** (`OFF` by default).
- Bank 0 loads the project's Sound slots (program 0 is SLOT 01); bank 1 loads an INIT Sound (0 ALGO, 1 MODAL, 2 TAPE, 3 VA).
- Bank select is read from CC 0, or from CC 32 when CC 0 is 0 or missing, and stays until the next bank select.
- A Part with unsaved edits loads without asking, and keeps its edits for a program change back to that Sound.
- The notes that follow a program change wait up to 40 ms for the new Sound.
- A program change heard while Chimera loads from the card, or while a prompt, learn or the Part's Sound browser is open, waits and lands when it closes.

### MIDI OUT and ECHO

- DIN MIDI OUT sends.
- Chimera sends a binding's value back to the controller on its own control when it changes, so LED rings and motor faders follow.
- New SETTINGS › MIDI CONFIG › ECHO, `ON` by default, switches everything Chimera sends.
- Each binding has its own ECHO (F on MIDI MAP); learn turns it on for relative encoders and 14-bit controls.
- A Part change, a Sound load and a project load send the Part's values all at once.
- ECHO can stay on when MIDI OUT loops back to MIDI IN: an echo heard back within a quarter second is not taken as a turn.
- Chimera answers a MIDI identity request with its identity and firmware version.
- New on ECHO's page: PARAM OUT, `OFF` or `NRPN`. At `NRPN`, every cell you turn on the panel goes out of MIDI OUT and USB as its NRPN, on the Part's channel, so a DAW or sequencer can record your edits. Values that came in over MIDI, loads, ORBIT and modulation never go out, and the last value of a fast turn always goes out.

### Active Sensing

- Once a DIN controller sends Active Sensing, pulling its cable releases every held note and lifts its held sustain pedal within a third of a second.
- The screen then shows **DIN MIDI LOST**, and **USB MIDI LOST** when a USB host resets or sleeps while you hold a note or pedal.

### USB

- Chimera is a class-compliant USB device: no driver on Linux, macOS or Windows.
- It shows up as one MIDI port, **Chimera**, both ways, every channel, as on DIN. Learn, ECHO, clock, SysEx and the identity reply work over it.
- It also shows up as an audio input, **Chimera**: the main out in stereo, 24-bit, 48 kHz, what the synth plays into the main out jacks. Record it in your DAW; the jacks keep playing while it streams.
- And as an audio output, **Chimera**: your computer's sound, stereo, 24-bit, 48 kHz, mixed into the main out. Chimera sets the pace, so it never drifts or clicks over a long session. New SETTINGS › AUDIO ROUTING › USB AUDIO › USB IN sets how loud: `OFF`, `-24dB` up to `0dB` (the default). Recording from the unit never includes what the computer plays. At `0dB`, a loud computer track over a loud patch can clip the main out: turn one of them down.
- On Linux, PipeWire may start the new Chimera output at 40 % volume: set it to 100 % in your sound settings.
- A USB bus reset releases every note and pedal. A host going to sleep releases only what USB was holding, so a pad held from DIN keeps sounding.
- After a host that wasn't reading starts reading again, Chimera sends the current Part's values instead of old ones.

### Modulation

- The MOD matrix has three new source rows for your hands: WHEEL (the mod wheel), PRESS (aftertouch) and SLIDE (CC 74). The readout spells them MOD WHEEL, PRESSURE and SLIDE.
- PRESS follows the higher of channel pressure and the note's own poly pressure.
- The wheel, pressure and slide glide, so a fast wheel throw never steps the sound.
- Every LFO's DEPTH is a matrix destination: prime it with **MIX + PLUS** on the LFO page.
- A new Sound (INIT) routes WHEEL into LFO 1's DEPTH at +127, with LFO 1's DEPTH at 0, so the wheel plays vibrato, and moving it no longer marks the Part edited.
- CC 1 leaves the default MIDI map. Factory Sounds that move LFO 1 keep the wheel they were voiced with, a CC 1 binding on its DEPTH.
- ALGO's matrix fits its 13 source rows on one screen.

### Tuning

- Each Part plays its own tuning, picked at SETTINGS › AUDIO ROUTING › TUNING, cell B **TUNING**.
- TUNING offers `12-TET`, `JUST`, `PYTHAG`, `MEANTONE`, `WERCK`, `MTS`, and the Scala files on the card.
- Turning TUNING past `MTS` steps through the Scala files (`.scl`) in the card's `CHIMERA/TUNINGS` folder by file name, long names included; the line under the readout shows the scale's own name.
- A long file name scrolls in the big readout and the cell while TUNING has focus: it holds, runs to its end, holds, and starts again.
- The hidden files a Mac leaves on the card (`._…`, `.DS_Store`) are never listed.
- A `.kbm` keyboard map pairs with the scale of the same name.
- New cell C **MAPPING**: `CONTIN.` (continuous) or `KEYBD` (keyboard), how a Scala file lies on the keys. A `.kbm` file of the same name maps the keys instead.
- A missing or unreadable file plays `12-TET` and says why, such as `PELOG.SCL NOT FOUND` or `PELOG.SCL NOT SCALA`.
- `MTS` follows MIDI Tuning Standard SysEx from a DAW or editor: single-note, bulk dump and scale/octave messages.
- A new note plays the tuning; a sounding note keeps its pitch, and a gliding note eases into the new key's pitch.
- The PITCH page's tuner reads the note as the Part's tuning plays it.

### RANDOMIZE

- New SETTINGS › PART › RANDOMIZE rolls a new Sound on the Part, musical by construction.
- Four amounts set what it rolls: OSC (`OFF` `PURE` `RICH` `WILD`), ENV (`OFF` `PLUCK` `PAD` `ANY`), TONE (`OFF` `SOFT` `BRIGHT` `WILD`) and MOD (`OFF` `SUBTLE` `MOVING` `WILD`).
- Any turn rolls. SEED (0 to 255) gives the same Sound again when you turn back to it, and the hint reads `TURN  ROLLS THE SOUND`.
- A roll keeps the note's pitch and the Part's LEVEL, PITCH, sends, LFO 1 and the filter's TYPE and MODE, and never comes out silent or deafening.
- A roll is an edit: the Part reads `* EDITED`, and RELOAD FROM PROJ undoes it.
- SETTINGS › PART's list scrolls.

### Effects

- The chorus's cell is now TYPE, with two new TYPEs: FLANGER and PHASER.
- FLANGER is a short swept delay fed back on itself; PHASER sweeps six all-pass stages a side, fed back.
- RATE, DEPTH and MIX work on every TYPE, and changing TYPE never clicks.
- The send hint reads `CHORUS ▸ FLANGER` or `CHORUS ▸ PHASER`.

### Sound browser

- EDIT + a Part's button, and EDIT on a Part's mixer page, open the Sound browser on the PROJECT tab with the cursor on that Part's Sound.
- An INIT Part opens on its engine's INIT row.
- Going to MENU and back, or back from naming a LIBRARY save, returns to the tab you left.

### Voices and efficiency

- The delay, chorus and reverb cost nothing while nothing is sent to them and their tails have died, and unused output pairs skip their work. The sound is the same, bit for bit.
- ALGO, MODAL, TAPE, the filters and the envelopes run faster, with the same sound.
- Voice costs follow new readings on the unit: MODAL BOWED, VA MAX and PHASE, and very short TAPE loops cost less; VA AM and SOFT SYNC, the filter's FEEDBACK and a moving SEM filter cost a little more.
- The Voices table above is now taken from the firmware's own billing model, with ORBIT stopped. The 0.2 table was counted with more room held back, so the two don't compare row by row: the Sounds that really lost a voice are listed below.
- Each voice is now billed at the worst block the unit has measured for it, so a dense chord never runs out of time. In exchange, five factory Sounds play one voice fewer than in 0.2 (on their own, QUAD reverb, ORBIT stopped): DEAD RADIO 8 → 7, BIT SHRED 7 → 6, SERVO 6 → 5, GROWL BASS 6 → 5 and YELLING LEAD 5 → 4. Every other factory Sound keeps its count.

### Install and update

- `CHIMERA.BK2` now also holds ALGO, MODAL, the TAPE delay and the chorus. With it missing or out of date they are silent, and the screens read NEEDS UPDATE or UPDATE.
- With `CHIMERA.BK2` missing or out of date, MIDI in is ignored, MIDI MAP reads NEEDS UPDATE, and **MIX + SEQ** says NEEDS UPDATE.
- Saving with `CHIMERA.BK2` missing or out of date keeps the Parts' MIDI maps.
- RANDOMIZE's cells read NEEDS UPDATE with `CHIMERA.BK2` missing or out of date.
- A Sound whose MIDI map comes from a newer firmware loads without the map and says SOME PARAMS SKIPPED, instead of refusing the Sound.

### Fixes

- On ALGO, a held note with LPG and STRIKE up no longer falls silent: the gate follows the carriers' envelopes, and STRIKE and DECAY pluck over them.
- A sustain pedal held from DIN is lifted when the controller's Active Sensing stops, so pedal-held notes no longer keep sounding.
- The Sound browser opens on the Part's Sound and on the PROJECT tab, not on slot 1 of the last tab used.
- A CC sent during a LIBRARY save or a card listing is no longer dropped.
- The PITCH tuner reads the Part's tuning, not 12-TET.
- A controller map removed from the card no longer leaves its name on the Part, and `NONE` can be picked again.

## Something wrong?

- Check the [known issues](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases/blob/main/KNOWN-ISSUES.md).
- [Report a bug](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases/issues/new/choose).
- To go back to the stock firmware, see the [README](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases#switching-back-to-the-original-preenfm3-firmware).

name: Chimera 0.2.0 (alpha)
body:
# Chimera 0.2.0 (alpha)

New firmware for the PreenFM3: four sound engines (ALGO, MODAL, VA and TAPE), six parts, and the ORBIT sequencer. This is an early test version.

## What to download

- `CHIMERA.BIN`: the firmware.
- `CHIMERA.BK2`: the rest of the firmware (Chimera installs it from the card on its first start).
- `factory-v1.zip`: 128 sounds, the TAPE sources they play, and 4 demo songs.

## Install

The same steps install Chimera for the first time and update it from 0.1. The [README](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases#installing-chimera) has them with pictures.

1. Unzip `factory-v1.zip`. It unzips to one folder, **CHIMERA**.
2. Turn the PreenFM3 off. Hold **MENU** and turn it on: the bootloader should read `pfm3 BootLoader 1.09`.
3. Press **button 3** (SD card access). The card shows up on your computer like a USB stick. It stays inside the PreenFM3.
4. Copy `CHIMERA.BIN` and `CHIMERA.BK2` to the top of the card, not into a folder. If older copies are there, choose **Replace**.
5. Copy the factory set:
   - If the card has no **CHIMERA** folder, copy the whole unzipped **CHIMERA** folder onto it.
   - If it has one, copy folder by folder instead (on a Mac, replacing a whole folder throws away what was in it):
     - **SOUNDS** and **PROJECTS**: copy the files inside into the folders of the same name, choosing **Replace**.
     - **TAPES**: if the card has no TAPES folder (a card from 0.1 has none), copy the whole folder across. If it has one, copy the files inside and choose **Skip** for any `.SRC` file already there. A source's name is its contents' checksum, so the one on the card is the same, and Chimera keeps it read-only.
   - The demo songs take the first 4 project slots. If you saved songs of your own there, copy them to your computer first.
6. Eject the card on your computer and press **MENU** to leave SD card access.
7. Step through the files with **−** and **+** until the bootloader shows `CHIMERA.BIN`, and press **button 1** (flash).
8. Chimera starts, finds `CHIMERA.BK2` on the card and installs it. It shows **DON'T POWER OFF** while it steps through ERASING, WRITING and SEALING, then carries on by itself. If the power goes off during the install, the next start installs it again.

If `CHIMERA.BK2` is missing or from another version, TAPE, ORBIT, the reverbs and the other parts that need it make no sound, and their screens say **UPDATE** or **NEEDS UPDATE**. Copy the `CHIMERA.BK2` from this release onto the card and restart.

To find the sounds: press **EDIT + B1**, then turn **encoder 2** to the **FACTORY** tab.

### Coming from 0.1

- `CHIMERA.BK2` is now required. It is still one package, one flash and one install screen: copy both files in step 4 and flash `CHIMERA.BIN` as before.
- Copy the factory set in step 5 even if you copied 0.1's: it adds the TAPE Sounds and the TAPES folder with their sources.
- The bootloader is unchanged. Chimera still needs the stock bootloader 1.09 and never writes to it.

## Demo songs

- **REVERB ROOMS**: Turn TYPE through QUAD, ROOM and HALL.
- **REVERB BLOOM**: Hold slow chords, then turn TYPE from BLOOM to REVERSE.
- **REVERB GATE**: Play short, sharp notes: the gate cuts every tail, the echoes too.
- **CHORUS DELAY**: Turn CHORUS through I, II and I+II.

## Voices

Chimera has 8 voices in all, shared by the six Parts. Each note costs a share of the processor that depends on its Sound: the engine, the model, the filter and the FX slot. A note gets a voice only if its cost fits in what is left, so a light Sound plays all 8 and a heavy one fewer.

Voices one Part gets on its own, with the TAPE delay and the QUAD reverb:

| Sound type | Example | Voices |
|---|---|---|
| ALGO, one or two operators | DRIFT ORGAN | 7 |
| ALGO, typical | AIR RAID | 6 |
| ALGO, heaviest | SOFT HORNS | 3 |
| ALGO with formants | NULL CHOIR | 3 |
| VA on the 2040 | SOLO PORTA | 6 |
| VA with FUZZ | INIT VA, FX FUZZ | 5 |
| VA on the LADDER with FOLD | GROWL BASS | 5 |
| MODAL STRING | NYLON | 8 |
| MODAL BOWED | CELLO SWELL | 6 |
| MODAL BANK | GAMELAN | 2 |
| TAPE one-shot or loop | HARP HIT, PAD LOOP | 8 |
| TAPE STRETCH GRAIN | VOICE STRETCH | 5 |

The delay's GRAIN type and the ROOM, HALL and BLOOM reverbs cost about a voice: with one of them on, many Sounds play one voice fewer.

These counts are for the rev V chip (480 MHz). A rev Y chip runs at 400 MHz and has less to share, so heavier Sounds play fewer voices. SETTINGS › SYSTEM › ABOUT shows which chip yours has.

## What's new in 0.2

### Engines: TAPE

- New engine, TAPE. It plays sound sources from the SD card. Its chain is SRC › DECK › FLT › AMP › MOD.
- The Sound browser has an INIT TAPE row. TAPE Sounds load from the PROJECT, LIBRARY and FACTORY tabs like any other engine's.
- SRC page: SOURCE, START, END and VOL.
- START and END turn in time, 1 to 100 ms a detent, and read in ms.
- MIX + turn on START or END snaps to the next onset in the source. The focus band shows the hint.
- SOURCE's focus band shows the source's size and length, and how many notes of it can stream (for example `24K · 30.0 S · 7 STREAMS`).
- A source that fits in memory plays from memory. A longer one streams from the card while it plays.
- A machine that a streamed source can't play is shown dimmed, with the reason (`… NEEDS RAM · STREAMED`).
- A file that fails to read twice is marked BAD FILE. Only the notes reading it drop out; everything else keeps playing.
- MODEL picks the machine: WALK, STRETCH, SCRUB or WAVE. Turning MODEL writes that machine's defaults.
- Every machine's model page starts with the tape wear: TAPE, AGE and WOW.
- Every machine draws its own glyph in the focus band. The knobs drive it, and it stays still when nothing changes.
- With CHIMERA.BK2 missing or out of date, a TAPE Part still loads as TAPE, stays silent and reads NEEDS UPDATE.

#### WALK

- WALK, one machine for one-shots, loops, ping-pong and Mellotron-style tapes.
- DECK on WALK: MODEL, LENGTH, FADE, DIRECTION, POSITION and DRIFT.
- DIRECTION: FWD, REVERSE, LOOP or PING.
- DRIFT: at each note, POSITION moves by a random step of up to DRIFT, starting from where the last note left it.
- FADE's last step reads HOLD on FWD and REVERSE with TRON off.
- WALK page: TAPE, AGE, WOW, TRON, XFADE and RETRIG.
- XFADE and RETRIG dim where the current DIRECTION can't use them, and the focus band says why.
- RETRIG: STACK or CUT.
- TRON ON gives each key its own tape, 0.25 to 8 s long (LENGTH), the same at every pitch. The window comes round until the tape runs out. Key up lifts the pad.
- LENGTH reads in seconds when TRON is on.
- WALK's glyph is two runners on a straight lane. They face the way DIRECTION plays, run round a track on LOOP and back to back on PING. POSITION and LENGTH light the strip under them, FADE dashes its end, DRIFT changes their stride, and TRON puts a finish post where the tape runs out.

#### STRETCH

- STRETCH plays a source at the key's pitch, stretched or squeezed in time. TYPE picks CLASSIC or GRAIN.
- DECK on STRETCH: MODEL, TYPE, SPEED, LENGTH, D-TIME and POSITION. LENGTH is GRAIN's; D-TIME and POSITION are CLASSIC's. A TYPE's cells dim under the other TYPE.
- SPEED 0 freezes the sound in place.
- LENGTH (GRAIN): how long a key plays the source, 0.25 to 8 s.
- STRCH page: TAPE, AGE, WOW, GRAIN (30 to 250 ms), SPRAY and END (HOLD or STOP). The last three are GRAIN's.
- STRETCH GRAIN stays in tune at every LENGTH.
- STRETCH's glyph is an accordion under a note.

#### SCRUB

- SCRUB moves through a source by hand, like a tape reel under your finger.
- DECK on SCRUB: MODEL, FINGER, SPEED, LENGTH, XFADE and DRAG.
- FINGER's encoder works as a jog: it reads how fast you turn, then glides to a stop through DRAG when you let go. A CC or a MOD route moves it too.
- LENGTH is the loop behind the finger, 2 ms to 2 s. The default, 70 ms, makes the first FINGER turn audible.
- SCRUB page: TAPE, AGE, WOW and KEY.
- KEY POSITION (the default): each key places the finger. C is the start of the window, and each semitone up is 1/12 further along, the same in every octave. FINGER's focus band reads KEYS PLACE THE FINGER.
- KEY PITCH: the scrub plays at the key's pitch.
- SCRUB's glyph is a sponge.

#### WAVE

- WAVE plays wavetable sources. DECK on WAVE: MODEL, FRAME, SCAN and RANGE.
- WAVE's glyph is film running through a gate.

### Engines: VA

- New MODE FM: OSC 2 modulates OSC 1 through zero. BLEND's ends read CLEAN and DEEP.
- New MODE AM: OSC 2 changes OSC 1's level without inverting it. In the top third of BLEND it runs on into RING.
- New MODE MAX: the louder of the two waves at each moment, with its corners rounded. BLEND fades from MIX to MAX.
- New MODE LOOPFM: each oscillator feeds back on its own frequency. It is the cheapest MODE.
- New MODE SOFT SYNC (the cell reads SOFT): OSC 2 reverses direction at each OSC 1 cycle instead of resetting.
- New MODE PHASE: OSC 2 bends OSC 1's phase, as in phase distortion.
- MODE names read in full in the focus band.
- New NOISE page: KIND (WHITE, PINK, RED or DIGITAL) and LEVEL. The noise is mixed in beside SUB, before the filter.
- NOISE KIND DIGITAL steps 16 times each OSC 1 cycle, so it follows the key.
- The VA chain bar reads OSC1 · OSC2 · NOISE · PIT.
- STABILITY shows a spirit level in the focus band. The further the bubble sits from the middle, the more the voices drift.

### Engines: every engine

- PIT's scope has a tuner in its top-right corner. It shows the note and cents the Part's last note sounds at (`C4 +12ct`) over its frequency (`261.6 Hz`).
- The tuner follows PITCH and FINE as they turn, with no note held. It is lit while the Part sounds and dim between notes, and it reads `REF C4` before the first note.
- On TAPE, a source with no known pitch reads `ROOT ?` over its shift from the source's own speed.

### Filters

- New filter TYPE SEM, modelled on the Oberheim SEM-1A filter circuit.
- SEM's MODE is a knob: it sweeps from low-pass, through a notch at FREQ, to high-pass. MODE can be modulated.
- SEM's OUTPUT, on FLT › MOD, picks MODE (the knob's sweep) or BP (band-pass).
- New on the 2040, LADDER and SEM: STABILITY. Each voice gets its own slightly different chip: a cutoff offset, slow drift, a tracking error and a resonance spread.
- STABILITY sits on FLT › FX. New Sounds start halfway, a Prophet-like amount. Saved and factory Sounds play as before.
- New on every TYPE: FEEDBACK (cell FDBK). It feeds the filter's output back into its cutoff, positive or negative, in the manner of the Kobol Expander's Surfer. It is a MOD matrix destination.
- FEEDBACK has its own glyph: a filter curve with a loop from the output back to the cutoff.
- The 2040's Kobol Expander voicing now reads EXPNDR (it was EXP).
- EXPNDR keeps its bass at high resonance, as the Kobol does, and rings over a full-level input.
- FLT's front page, on every TYPE: TYPE, FX, Q, MODE, FX PLACE and FREQ. On the 2040: RES, VOICE and CUTOFF in their places — suggested by Lizard of Oz
- On the 2040, TYPE names its one mode, 4-POLE LP, and the fixed MODE cell is gone.
- FLT › MOD, on every TYPE: ENV AMT, KEYBOARD, FREQ MOD, FDBK and RES MOD, in plain names.
- New FLT › JACK page: FREQ SRC and RES SRC, the sources that FREQ MOD and RES MOD read.
- FREQ MOD and RES MOD name their routed source in the focus band, for example `FREQ MOD LFO1`.
- FLT's picture draws each filter's real response. The resonance peak no longer shows too high at low RES — suggested by Lizard of Oz
- The band-pass and notch shapes are also drawn from the filter's real response.
- FLT's CUTOFF and RES numbers and curve show the value you set. Modulation shows separately, as a faint mark beside them — suggested by Lizard of Oz

### FX slot (drive, fuzz and fold)

- Every voice has one FX slot in its filter: TYPE OFF, SOFT, FUZZ or FOLD.
- FX PLACE puts the effect before (PRE) or after (POST) the filter.
- New FLT › FX page: INPUT, the TYPE's three controls, and MIX.
- SOFT: DRIVE, TONE and LEVEL.
- New FUZZ, modelled on the Big Muff's circuit: SUSTAIN, TONE and VOLUME. It starts at PRE.
- FOLD: FOLD, SYMMETRY and LEVEL.
- The FX PLACE cell shows a small glyph of the order: FX into FLT, or FLT into FX.
- FLT › FX's focus band draws the signal path (for example `VA › FUZZ › FLT`) and the effect's curve: a sine going in, the shaped wave coming out.
- The four TYPEs are level-matched, and changing TYPE or PLACE fades over 20 ms, with no click.
- In the MOD matrix, the FOLD column is now FX. In the matrix and the MIDI map, FX cells are named by their TYPE (DRIVE, SUSTAIN, FOLD and so on).
- The DRV page and AMP's fold cells are gone. Sounds made with them load into the FX slot at the same loudness: DRV as SOFT PRE, the fold as FOLD POST. A Sound that used both keeps its DRV and drops the fold.

### AMP and LPG

- The VCA can now act as a low-pass gate. AMP reads VEL, LPG, DECAY and STRIKE.
- LPG ties the tone to the level: the quieter the sound, the darker it is.
- DECAY sets how slowly the gate closes.
- STRIKE pings the gate at each note, as hard as the note is played.
- With an envelope routed to the VCA, STRIKE is an accent on top of it: the envelope is never turned down, and a held note stays at its level after each strike.
- With LPG, DECAY and STRIKE all at 0, AMP is the plain VCA, exactly as before.
- LPG, DECAY and STRIKE can be modulated and MIDI-mapped.
- The send levels moved to AMP › SENDS, the same page as the mixer's SENDS.

### Effects

- The delay has a TYPE: TAPE (as before) or GRAIN.
- New GRAIN delay, in the manner of Mutable Instruments' Beads. The GRAIN page holds SIZE, DENSITY, PITCH and TEXTURE.
- The delay's CHAR page is heard under TAPE, and its GRAIN page under GRAIN.

### UI and navigation

- New sub-page panel under the chain map — suggested by Lizard of Oz
- The sub-page panel underlines the current page in the accent colour and shows `<` and `>` when more pages lie off either edge. Every sub-page is on screen, including MOD's envelopes and LFOs.
- Six Part dots in the top-left corner show which Part you're on — suggested by Lizard of Oz
- The current Part's dot is bright green, a Part that is sounding has a ring, and the rest are faint.
- A value shows its new number as soon as you stop turning. Only the arcs and bars ease, and the sound still glides — suggested by Lizard of Oz
- Any encoder moves the highlight in SETTINGS, the project lists, the Sound browser and the prompts — suggested by Lizard of Oz
- In every dialog, EDIT confirms and MENU or SEQ cancels. The legends read EDIT OK and MENU BACK — suggested by Lizard of Oz
- Prompts that delete or overwrite open with CANCEL highlighted.
- Mixer cells show the hint `MIX + B1-6 PART`, and mappable cells add `MIX + SEQ LEARN` — suggested by Lizard of Oz
- With ALG A or ALG B focused, the picture shows that algorithm, not the morph between them — suggested by Lizard of Oz
- WAVE lists every waveform on every operator, and ALG A and ALG B list every algorithm. One that can't be used is shown dimmed, with the reason in the focus band (for example `OP n MODULATED · OVER BUDGET`).
- The focus band shows a big number with a small unit, and the arc never covers the value.
- LFO pages draw the LFO itself in the scope: one cycle at its set values, with a dot riding the newest voice's phase.
- Each LFO control has its own glyph: RATE, SHAPE, SYNC, PHASE, DEPTH, TILT, DELTA and SLEW.
- CLASSIC LFO RATE reads in Hz. CLASSIC PHASE is dimmed under FREE.
- FUNC RATE tops out at 93.75 Hz. Older Sounds set higher load at that limit.
- A MIDI CC move shows on its cell within about 200 ms, as fast as it sounds.
- A touch that wakes the screen saver now acts. A waking encoder turn skips its first detent, so the value doesn't jump.
- MIDI MAP's hints show which encoder sets CC, MIN and MAX.

### SETTINGS

- New: PERSONALIZE › CHAIN MAP › PAGES, ROW (the sub-page panel, the default) or STACK (the old vertical list).
- New: PERSONALIZE › TEXT SIZE › SIZE, NORMAL or LARGE. LARGE draws labels, values, hints, SETTINGS rows and Sound names a size up — suggested by Lizard of Oz
- SCREENSAVER: new steps of 2, 5 and 10 minutes, and the default is now 5 minutes — suggested by Lizard of Oz

### Sounds and library

- 16 dark industrial ALGO Sounds: RUST REESE, IRON SUB, EBM PULSE, GRIND BASS, BILE LEAD, RING SIREN, NASAL MONO, DEAD CHOIR, RUST PAD, AIR RAID, AGGRO STAB, BLACK BRASS, GIRDER, SERVO, CRACK SNARE and DEAD RADIO.
- 16 more ALGO Sounds built on MORPH, inharmonic ratios and broken textures: SHARD LEAD, BROKEN WIRE, HEX VOICE, NULL CHOIR, BLACK SUN, SODIUM HAZE, SIGNAL ROT, TORN BASS, BENT BASS, MOTOR BASS, RIOT STAB, ASH CHORD, TIN CAN, BIT SHRED, SPARK GAP and SONAR VOID.
- New VA Sounds: THE RIGHT PLACE, VELVET FOG, AMBER GLIDE, SYNC VOICE, FLUTTER KEYS, STEPPED RAIN, PIXEL PLUCK and GRAIN SWARM.
- 32 TAPE Sounds: SINE LOOP, EPIANO HIT, EPIANO STAB, STAB STRETCH, TX BASS HIT, SQR BASS HIT, BRASS LOOP, BELL HIT, BELL BACKWARDS, SAW SCRUB, PAD LOOP, PAD PINGPONG, KEYS LOOP, PLUCK HIT, PLUCK LOW, HARP HIT, BOWED LOOP, BOWED STRETCH, METAL HIT, GLASS HIT, SYMP LOOP, TRON BOWED, NOISE LOOP, WIND LOOP, RAIN SCRUB, VOICE LOOP, VOICE STRETCH, WAVE MORPH, WAVE SAW, WAVE BOWED, WAVE BRASS and TINZ.
- 27 TAPE sources for them: 26 rendered from Chimera's own engines or synthesised, plus one CC0 voice recording.
- The factory set grows from 56 to 128 Sounds.
- NEW's built-in Sounds include INIT TAPE.
- The built-in Sounds that used DRV (SQR BASS, TALK BASS and VOX) now use the FX slot and sound as before.
- Factory Sounds that use SOFT or FOLD in the FX slot play at the level they were voiced at.

### Install and update

- The firmware now comes as two files, `CHIMERA.BIN` and `CHIMERA.BK2`. Their short names are easier to pick out in the bootloader's list than `CHIMER~1.BIN`.
- `CHIMERA.BK2` is now required. TAPE, the reverbs, FUZZ, FEEDBACK, SEM, the LPG, NOISE, the GRAIN delay and several VA MODEs play from it.
- It is still one package, one flash and one install screen. On its first start Chimera installs `CHIMERA.BK2` from the card by itself and shows DON'T POWER OFF and INSTALLING while it steps through ERASING, WRITING and SEALING.
- If the power goes during the install, the next start runs the install again.
- While `CHIMERA.BK2` is missing or out of date, the parts that need it are silent and read UPDATE or NEEDS UPDATE.
- ORBIT plays from `CHIMERA.BK2`.

### USB console

- New console commands `key` and `turn` press buttons and turn encoders over USB, for testing without hands on the panel.

### Fixes

- A swept MIDI CC now lands exactly on the mapped MIN and MAX, stepped and inverted too.
- Long values such as `2.14 kHz` no longer run under the arc in the focus band.
- An operator that can't be a formant now says why (the formant budget), instead of the turn silently skipping it.
- The ALGO picture redraws when ALG A or ALG B is focused or changed.
- The 2040 and LADDER now count their real cost on the chip.
- Voice costs are the ones measured on the unit. FUZZ counts at its real cost, and a TAPE loop counts by its length, so the factory loops get all 8 voices.
- A STRETCH GRAIN chord struck on eight keys at once no longer overruns the audio block.
- A TAPE source copied onto the card by hand is checked and sealed the first time it streams. A damaged one is refused.

## Something wrong?

- Check the [known issues](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases/blob/main/KNOWN-ISSUES.md).
- [Report a bug](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases/issues/new/choose).
- To go back to the stock firmware, see the [README](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases#switching-back-to-the-original-preenfm3-firmware).

name: Chimera 0.1.0
body:
# Chimera 0.1.0 (alpha)

New firmware for the PreenFM3: three sound engines, six parts, and the ORBIT sequencer. This is an early test version.

## What to download

- `chimera-0.1.0.bin`: the firmware.
- `factory-v1.zip`: 56 sounds and 4 demo songs.

## 1. Install the firmware

Follow the short steps in the [README](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases#install).

## 2. Add the sounds

1. Unzip `factory-v1.zip`.
2. Turn the PreenFM3 off. Hold **MENU** and turn it on.
3. Press **button 3** (SD card access). The PreenFM3 shows up on your computer like a USB stick.
4. Copy the **CHIMERA** folder onto it. If your computer asks, choose **merge** or **replace**.
5. Eject it on your computer. Turn the PreenFM3 off and on again.

The demo songs replace any song saved in the first four slots.

To find the sounds: press **EDIT + B1**, then turn **knob 2** to the **FACTORY** tab.

## Demo songs

- **REVERB ROOMS**: Turn TYPE through QUAD, ROOM and HALL.
- **REVERB BLOOM**: Hold slow chords, then turn TYPE from BLOOM to REVERSE.
- **REVERB GATE**: Play short, sharp notes: the gate cuts every tail, the echoes too.
- **CHORUS DELAY**: Turn CHORUS through I, II and I+II.

## Something wrong?

- Check the [known issues](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases/blob/main/KNOWN-ISSUES.md).
- [Report a bug](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases/issues/new/choose).
- To go back to the stock firmware, see the [README](https://github.com/joegiralt/chimera-releases#go-back-to-the-stock-firmware).
